newsitem.title: GERMANY: Higher reserves help German call money rates ease.
newsitem.headline: Higher reserves help German call money rates ease.

text.p: German overnight rates eased slightly on Friday as the market appeared less concerned with monthly reserve requirements, realising there was still plenty of time to fulfil more of their obligations later in the month.
"You could call the market slightly more relaxed, although I would not go so far as to call it very much softer," said a senior trader at a major Frankfurt-based bank.

Call money traded in a narrow range between 3.10/3.125 percent on Friday morning after trading in a 3.125/3.15 percent range on Thursday, and some traders expected to see still lower rates this afternoon. "We could go to 3.05 percent," one said.

Dealers explained a slight change in attitude about meeting monthly reserve requirements might have triggered the relaxation. Additionally cash has flowed back into the system since the Easter holiday and funds were offered at around 3.0625 percent in the Euromarket, dealers said.
"The monthly reserve numbers look fairly good, we are already above the month's requirement and so the situation is a bit more relaxed now," another trader added.
The Bundesbank sets the reserve requirement near the end of the month, but traders have predicted it would be between 40.6 and 40.8 billion marks for April.
On Thursday banks held 42.1 billion marks at the Bundesbank after holding 41.7 billion marks on Wednesday. But the monthly average slipped to 42.8 billion marks from 43.2 billion marks.

Call money rates have been stubbornly stuck around the 3.10 percent level for several weeks as the Bundesbank has kept its main money market rate, the repo, steady at three percent for over seven months.

Dealers said the market's undertone became even firmer amid nervousness that Germany's central bank might be forced to raise rates sooner than later, after last week's U.S. short-term interest rate hike.

Dealers feared rates would remain stuck at higher levels as long as uncertainty about the direction of interest rates remained. But several dealers said this view was no longer as prevalent today, especially after the Bundesbank left all key rates steady on Thursday, meeting broad market expectations.
Before the weekend dealers also said that Thursday's concerns about pulling forward their need to fulfil reserve requirements might have been overstated a bit.
Traditionally dealers often expect to see cheaper rates at the end of the month and postpone fulfilling their obligations as long as possible.
On Friday the Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average was set at 3.13433 percent, down from Thursday's 3.15400 percent rate.
